subject: Clarifying data residency & retention: request vs. outputs
messages:
From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@datacorp.com>

Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@datacorp.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency / retention questions for audit

Hi Naomi,

Hope you're well. We're preparing for an upcoming SOC 2 readiness review and our security team asked for clarification on Redwood's default logging/retention behavior. A few specific asks: 

- By default, does Redwood retain the raw request (user prompt) and the model response (generated output) for hosted accounts? If so, for how long?
- How do streaming tokens / partially streamed outputs factor into retention? Are intermediate fragments persisted anywhere?
- For EU-residency customers we may need proof of deletion — what is your evidence/workflow when a customer requests erasure?
- What attachments or artifacts (e.g., request metadata, headers, model id, kv-cache snapshots) are treated as persistent logs vs ephemeral buffers?

We'd like short bullets and any links to runbooks or artifacts we can hand to our audit team. If you prefer to loop in legal/compliance, happy to include them.

Thanks — appreciate a quick clarification.

Best,
Ava Reynolds
Head of Security Programs
DataCorp

(Attachment: DataCorp_SOW.pdf)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency / retention questions for audit

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary below, I followed with a detailed note and a few links. Looping in legal for one line confirmation.

Short answers (hosted API default):
- Default retention: requests (prompts) and final responses are retained for 30 days by default.
- Streaming fragments: buffered only transiently for delivery (<= 1 hour) and not written to persistent logs unless the request is configured to persist or the SDK/client asks to capture the final output.
- KV-cache and ephemeral session state: never persisted to customer-facing logs by default; used in-memory on the serving runtime and flushed on pod recycle.
- Evidence & erasure: customers may request account-level deletion via support; we run a deletion job that returns a signed job id and timestamp (we can provide a deletion evidence package).

Details and links: 
- Retention windows can be extended for Dedicated/Private deployments or by enabling "persisted logs" in account settings.
- For EU residency, we support region-scoped storage and will ensure deletion is executed in the resident region when requested.
- Standard artifacts we retain by default: request text, final model response, model identifier, request metadata (api key id, timestamp, route). We do NOT persist streaming incremental tokens nor KV cache snapshots.
- Runbook: https://redwood-inference.internal/kb/retention-policy (attached summary PDF).

I'll attach a concise one-pager and include legal for precise wording around deletion evidence.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Exec, Strategic Sales

Hi all — legal & privacy here. Confirming and tightening Naomi's bullets for audit deliverables. Please see the redlined points below; I'm sending this back to DataCorp as the official wording.

Official wording for auditors (short bullet list):
- Persistence defaults (hosted): By default, Redwood retains request inputs (prompts) and final model outputs for 30 days. This applies to standard hosted accounts unless account settings are changed to enable longer retention.
- Streaming tokens and transient buffers: Intermediate streaming fragments (partial token buffers) are held in-memory only for the duration of the request delivery pipeline (typically under 1 hour) and are not written to persistent storage by default.
- Ephemeral runtime state: KV-cache and model serving caches are in-memory artifacts used to accelerate inference and are not recorded to customer logs or long-term storage.
- Residency behavior: When a customer requests EU residency or selects a region-scoped plan, stored artifacts (requests, final outputs, metadata) are kept exclusively in that region's storage by default. Deletion requests are executed within the selected region.
- Deletion evidence and workflow: Customers submit an erasure request via the support portal or their account manager. Redwood initiates a coordinated deletion job that: (1) removes persisted artifacts from primary storage; (2) schedules background purge of replicas and backups per the backup retention policy; and (3) issues a signed deletion report containing job id, timestamp, operator id, and affected object identifiers. For audits, Redwood provides the signed deletion report and a summary of the purge job.

Notes & recommended customer asks: include your account id and the approximate time window you want erased to speed processing. If you require retention longer than the hosted default for business reasons, we recommend Dedicated capacity with explicit retention windows documented in the SOW.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference
